newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela reviews scheduled visit to Middle East.
newsitem.headline: Mandela reviews scheduled visit to Middle East.

text.p: South Africa said on Thursday that President Nelson Mandela would review a scheduled visit to the Middle East next month pending progress in top-level talks to revive the flagging peace process.
"The in-principal decision to go is in place, and the dates are still the same. But the president will be reviewing progress in the peace talks," a foreign affairs official told Reuters.
"The key word is 'review', and the outcome of talks between the Palestinian and Israeli delegations planned for Sunday will be an indicator," the official said.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators are due to meet in Gaza at the weekend to discuss Israel's long-delayed troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron, following an inconclusive leaders' summit in Washington this week.
Earlier on Thursday, Mandela said that he wanted to visit the Middle East as planned next month, and would urge the Israeli and Palestinian leaders to sort out their differences.

"I plan to go and talk to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and President Yasser Arafat, because whatever problems you have, you reach a stage where none of the parties are totally correct or totally wrong," he said.
"That is the situation which has been reached in the Middle East," he told reporters after meeting the South African Jewish Board of Deputies in Pretoria.

"My message to them is going...to be, 'When historians record what happened in Israel and Palestine they are going to say that the troubles occurred when the two of you were leaders. That will be the indictment of history'."
Fifty-eight Palestinians and 15 Israelis died in five days of clashes after Israel opened a tunnel to archaeological sites near Jerusalem's temple mount, sacred to Moslems and Jews.

Mandela's first visit to Israel, Palestinian territories, Jordan and Egypt was twice postponed from August and then October, officially in order to lengthen the visit. No details of his itinerary have been released as yet.
